label: Item itself

details: The game documents no return type and no vanilla text uses it on this type. Other types have a `Self` function that is passed to other functions, for example as the character in `GetTrait('chaste').GetName( recipient.Self )`; that is only a hint here.

label: Photo preset itself
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the photo preset itself; mostly handed to other functions.

label: Preset name
summary: The display name of a photo preset in the barbershop.
details: Vanilla uses it as the `text` of a widget in the barbershop window.

label: Preset tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of a photo preset in the barbershop.
details: Vanilla sets it as the `tooltip` of the preset's widget in the barbershop window.

label: Preset type
summary: Going by its use, an identifier of a photo preset that other barbershop functions accept.
details: Vanilla passes it to `BarbershopWindow.SetPhotoPreset` when a preset is clicked and to `BarbershopWindow.IsPhotoPresetSelected` to pick the button frame. The game does not name its return type.

label: Photo preset itself
summary: Going by its name, the photo preset itself, handed on as a value.
details: No vanilla line uses it on this type. Other types' `Self` is passed to other functions (for example `BarterMission.Self` goes to `DefaultOnBarterClick`); that is only a hint here.

label: Portrait itself
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the barbershop portrait itself; mostly handed to other functions.
details: No vanilla line uses it on this type. Other types' `AccessSelf` appears as an argument, such as `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf`; that is only a hint.

label: Portrait position
summary: Going by its name, the on-screen position of a portrait in the barbershop, as a two-part (x, y) value.
details: Vanilla uses it as the `position` of a widget in the barbershop window, in three places.

label: Portrait is a baby
summary: Going by its name, whether the portrait shows a baby.
details: Vanilla combines it with `IsBeingHovered` and `BarbershopWindow.HasPortraitShadow` to decide whether some widgets are visible. Which widgets is not shown in the input.

label: Portrait is hovered
summary: Going by its name, whether the mouse is currently over the portrait.
details: Vanilla uses it alone or together with `IsBaby` as a `visible` condition in the barbershop window. `SetBeingHovered` is called when the mouse enters and leaves, so it is likely what changes it.

label: Portrait itself
summary: Going by its name, the portrait itself, handed on as a value.
details: No vanilla line uses it on this type. Other types' `Self` is passed to other functions; that is only a hint here.

label: Set portrait hovered
summary: Tells the portrait whether the mouse is over it, going by its name and use.
details: Vanilla calls it with `yes` when the mouse enters the widget hierarchy (`onmousehierarchyenter`) and with `no` when it leaves. It returns nothing.

label: Should reset position
summary: Going by its name, whether the portrait's position should be reset.
details: Vanilla uses it as a `trigger_when` condition in the barbershop window. The input does not show what the trigger does.

label: Should stack on top
summary: Going by its name, whether the portrait should be stacked above other widgets.
details: Vanilla uses it as a `trigger_when` condition in the barbershop window, next to `StackWindowOnTop`. The input does not show more.

label: Stack window on top
summary: Going by its name, moves the given widget to the top of the stack of windows.
details: Vanilla calls it when a widget starts (`on_start`) and passes the widget itself with `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf`. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The widget to put on top.

label: Filtered pose list

label: Pose drop-down itself

label: Pose item itself

label: Pose name

summary: Going by its name, runs when the user finishes typing in the pose search box.

fields.text: Index of the pose under the mouse.

label: Leave screenshot mode

details: Vanilla calls it from `on_finish` in the barbershop window, in two places. It returns nothing.

label: Screenshot being taken

label: Screenshot button visible
summary: Going by its name, whether the screenshot button is shown.

label: Screenshot mode active

label: Screenshot notice visible

label: Show/hide UI notice visible

label: Screenshot notice finished
summary: Going by its name, runs when the screenshot notice has finished showing.
details: Vanilla calls it from `on_finish` in the barbershop window. It returns nothing.

label: Show/hide UI notice finished
summary: Going by its name, runs when the show/hide interface notice has finished showing.

details: Vanilla calls it from the click of a button in the barbershop window. It returns nothing.

details: Vanilla calls it from the click of two buttons in the barbershop window. It returns nothing.

label: Accessory categories

label: Background category
summary: Going by its name, the category of backgrounds, given to widgets as their data.

label: Background items
summary: Going by its name, the list of backgrounds the barbershop offers.

label: Barbershop characters

label: Color picker handler

label: Current background

label: Main character

label: Portrait shadow scale
summary: Going by its name, the scale of the portraits' shadow, as a decimal number.

label: Pose drop-down

details: Vanilla uses it as a `datacontext`. The game does not name its return type.

label: Has changes

label: Scene tab shown
summary: Going by its name, whether the scene tab of the barbershop is the one shown.

label: Reset appearance tab
summary: Going by its name, sets the appearance tab back to its starting state.
details: Vanilla calls it from a click in the barbershop window. It returns nothing.

label: Reset portrait positions

label: Reset scene tab

label: Daily barter progress

details: No vanilla line uses it; the game documents nothing more.

label: Battle side itself
summary: Going by its name, the battle result side itself, handed on as a value.
details: No vanilla line uses it on this type. Other types' `Self` is passed to other functions; that is only a hint here.

label: Battle summary itself
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the battle summary window itself; mostly handed to other functions.
details: No vanilla line uses it on this type. Other types' `AccessSelf` appears as an argument, such as `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf`; that is only a hint.

label: After dismissing
summary: Going by its name, runs after the battle summary was dismissed.
details: Vanilla calls it from `on_finish` in the battle summary window. It returns nothing.

label: Close battle summary
summary: Closes the battle summary window.
details: Vanilla calls it from a click on a button. The name `Close` exists on many window types.

label: Dismiss battle summary
summary: Going by its name, dismisses the battle summary.
details: Vanilla calls it from a click on a button in the battle summary window. `AfterDismiss` appears to follow it. It returns nothing.

label: Battle events
summary: The list of events (for example kills, wounds) the battle summary shows.
details: Vanilla uses it as the `datamodel` of a list widget, so the widget repeats per event. Its items are `BattleEvent` entries going by the surrounding functions. The game does not name its return type.

label: Left-side bonus
summary: Going by its name, a bonus number of the left side for the given men-at-arms type.
details: Vanilla passes `MenAtArmsType.Self` and compares the whole number with 1, 2 and 3 to show one of three widgets (for example `EqualTo_int32( ..., '(int32)2' )`). `GetBonusRight` is the same for the right side.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The men-at-arms type to look up.

label: Right-side bonus
summary: Going by its name, a bonus number of the right side for the given men-at-arms type.
details: Vanilla passes `MenAtArmsType.Self` and compares the whole number with 1, 2 and 3 to show one of three widgets. `GetBonusLeft` is the same for the left side.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The men-at-arms type to look up.

label: Combat result data
summary: The combat result of the battle, with the war contribution and gold gained.
details: Vanilla reads from it `GetWarContribution( GetPlayer )`, `PlayerGotGold` and `GetPlayerGoldGain`. It returns a `CombatResultData` object.

label: Battle end date
summary: Going by its name, the date the battle ended, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as the `text` of a widget in the battle summary.

label: Event sequence
summary: Going by its name, the list of events that concern one character in the battle.
details: Vanilla passes the right-side character from `BattleEvent.GetRightCharacter( ... )` and uses the result as a `datamodel`. The game does not name its return type.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character whose events are listed.

label: Event sequence size text
summary: Going by its name, a short text with the number of events in that character's sequence.
details: Vanilla passes the right-side character and puts it after `BattleEvent.GetTitle` in a text.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character whose event sequence is counted.

label: Knight kills
summary: Going by its name, how many kills a knight has in this battle, as a number.
details: Vanilla passes the left or right character of the battle event and shows the number after a colon, with no decimals (`|0`).

label: Knights sort index
summary: Going by its name, which sort option of the knights list is selected, as a two-part value.
details: Vanilla uses it as the `selectedindex` of a sort control; `GetKnightsSortOptions` gives the options.

label: Knights sort options
summary: Going by its name, the list of ways the knights list can be sorted.
details: Vanilla uses it as the `datamodel` of a sort control. The game does not name its return type.

label: Left army stretch
summary: Going by its name, how much room the left army gets in the summary's layout, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla uses it as `layoutstretchfactor_horizontal`, which divides width between widgets in a row.

label: Left side counters
summary: Going by its name, the list of men-at-arms types that the given type counters on the left side.
details: Vanilla passes `MenAtArmsType.Self` and uses the result as a `datamodel`, in three places. The input does not say what the list contains. The game does not name its return type.

label: Left side countered by
summary: Going by its name, the list of men-at-arms types that counter the given type on the left side.
details: Vanilla passes `MenAtArmsType.Self` and uses the result as a `datamodel`, in three places. The input does not say what the list contains. The game does not name its return type.

label: Left knights
summary: The list of the left side's knights with their statistics in the battle.
details: Vanilla uses it as a `datamodel` and counts it with `GetDataModelSize` for the header "N knights" and for "Your ... (N)". The game does not name its return type.

label: Left-side commander
summary: Going by its name, the commander of the left side, as a character.
details: No line uses it on this type. `CombatWindow.GetLeftSideCommander` is used as a `datacontext` in the combat window; that is only a hint.

label: Left commander tooltip
summary: Going by its name, the tooltip text for the left side's commander.
details: Vanilla uses it as a `tooltip` in the battle summary window.

label: Left-side main participant
summary: Going by its name, the main character on the left side of the battle, as a character.
details: Vanilla uses it as a `datacontext`, followed by `.GetCulture.GetGraphicalUnitType`, and in the text "Your [knight culture plural] ..." (`Custom('KnightCulturePlural')`).
